facts.raw_span: A man in his 40s
weighing 109kg
stage IV KRAS wild-type rectal adenocarcinoma diagnosed in November 2013
pulmonary and liver metastases
radiation therapy and multiple chemotherapy cycles
a single, well-defined, blanchable bright red plaque densely composed of telangiectasias on his lower right lateral shin
the lesion was not associated with pain or pruritus
Discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels were observed, with superficial, small lobules of small-caliber vessels
the epidermis was normal
KDR (VEGFR2) c.C2312G, p.T771R identified as the only somatic mutation

concepts.why: The presence of a bright red plaque densely composed of telangiectasias, discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels, and a somatic mutation in the KDR (VEGFR2) gene are consistent with angiosarcoma.
The appearance of a single, well-defined, blanchable bright red plaque densely composed of telangiectasias is consistent with cherry angioma, although the size and growth rate are unusual.

The presence of a bright red plaque densely composed of telangiectasias and discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels is consistent with pyogenic granuloma, although the lack of pain or pruritus is unusual.

The appearance of a bright red plaque densely composed of telangiectasias is consistent with bacillary angiomatosis, although the lack of systemic symptoms and the presence of a somatic mutation in the KDR (VEGFR2) gene are unusual.

The presence of a bright red plaque densely composed of telangiectasias and discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels is consistent with Kaposi's sarcoma, although the lack of systemic symptoms and the presence of a somatic mutation in the KDR (VEGFR2) gene are unusual.
It explains the development of a vascular lesion in a patient with a history of rectal adenocarcinoma and multiple chemotherapy cycles.

rationales.F06: The presence of a single, well-defined, blanchable bright red plaque densely composed of telangiectasias is more typical of Cutaneous Collateral Vessel Formation and Angiosarcoma.
rationales.F08: The histopathological finding of discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels with superficial, small lobules of small-caliber vessels is more typical of Angiosarcoma and Cutaneous Collateral Vessel Formation.
rationales.F10: The presence of a KDR (VEGFR2) c.C2312G, p.T771R somatic mutation is more typical of Angiosarcoma and Cutaneous Collateral Vessel Formation.
